$comment: Stable rule IDs. Never renumber or reuse an ID; retire one with "retired": true. "by" names the enforcers: a lint rule, standards:<check> (check:repository-standards), check:<step>, extension:<name>, react-doctor, fallow, or review (people and the standards-reviewer).

TS-01.rule: A tsconfig change only checks more: no source file leaves every project and no strictness flag weakens.

TS-02.rule: No raw type assertions except `as const`.

TS-03.rule: Use `satisfies`, annotations, generics, type guards, discriminated unions and Effect Schema instead of casts.

TS-04.rule: Use @total-typescript/shoehorn only in tests, for partial mocks or intentionally invalid inputs.

TS-05.rule: No `any`, `as unknown as`, `as never`, handler casts, `Record<string, unknown>` casts or `// SAFETY:` comments; no unsafe flow from untyped values.

TS-06.rule: Validate runtime inputs at boundaries with the Effect Schema helpers in src/shared/schema.ts and src/shared/schemas/.

TS-07.rule: No silent parse fallbacks; log structured context or surface a visible error.

TS-08.rule: No inline suppressions: eslint-disable, oxlint-disable, biome-ignore, fallow-ignore, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, @ts-nocheck. Fix the code or the shared config.

TS-09.rule: Prefer @diegogbrisa/ts-match for multi-branch discriminants, shape guards and boundary assertions; plain TypeScript for simple guards.

TS-10.rule: Avoid inline `import()` types; import types at the top of the file.

ARCH-01.rule: Main-process domain code is pure: no Electrobun, Node fs/process, SQL, Pi SDK or store imports.

ARCH-02.rule: Ports are Effect service interfaces with no vendor SDKs or stores.

ARCH-03.rule: Application services orchestrate through ports, with no direct store, IPC or Pi SDK imports.

ARCH-04.rule: IPC handlers are transport only: decode input, call an application service, return DTOs.

ARCH-05.rule: Stores are persistence details behind ports and services.

ARCH-07.rule: Fire-and-forget IPC calls handle their rejection.

ARCH-08.rule: No `typeof api.*` guards; preload members always exist.

PKG-01.rule: packages/extension-sdk stays browser-safe: no Electrobun, Node built-ins, Pi SDK, renderer stores, main services or app internals.

PKG-02.rule: packages/waggle-core stays runtime-neutral: no Pi SDK, Electrobun, Node built-ins, renderer stores or app services.

PKG-03.rule: packages/extension-react may use @openwaggle/extension-sdk and React peers only: no renderer components, app CSS, Tailwind internals, Electrobun or app services.

PKG-04.rule: packages/pi-waggle may import Pi SDKs but not Electrobun, renderer stores or app services.

PI-01.rule: App Pi SDK imports live under src/main/adapters/pi/; packages/pi-* may import Pi SDKs.

PI-02.rule: Keep Pi-native session, tool, provider, model, auth, thinking-level and compaction semantics end to end; OpenWaggle is not a parallel runtime.

PI-03.rule: Translate Pi details into OpenWaggle DTOs only at adapter boundaries.

PI-04.rule: Add tool or runtime layers only as Pi-native extensions behind ports.

PI-05.rule: Provider, model and auth metadata come from Pi through ports, never a parallel registry.

PI-06.rule: Project resources resolve .openwaggle > .pi > .agents; project config is .openwaggle/settings.json with Pi settings under `pi`.

PI-07.rule: Portable Waggle policy goes in packages/waggle-core; Pi-specific Waggle behavior in packages/pi-waggle.

SHELL-01.rule: Main-process environment access goes through src/main/env.ts.

SHELL-02.rule: Child processes get their environment from the env helpers, never a spread of process.env.

SHELL-03.rule: Native modules target Bun's Node ABI; verify packaging-only bugs in a packaged build.

SHELL-04.rule: Main-process code logs through structured loggers, not raw console.* outside logger modules.

SHELL-05.rule: Automated runs route window show/focus, dialogs and external apps through the automation policy.

SHELL-06.rule: Only src/main/adapters/electrobun/ and the preload transport import Electrobun.

REACT-01.rule: No React.memo, React.FC or forwardRef; the React Compiler handles memoization.

REACT-02.rule: useMemo and useCallback only for identity an external API needs, not render optimization.

REACT-03.rule: Prefer focused Zustand selectors and feature-owned hooks over prop-drilled controller objects.

REACT-04.rule: Renderer features live in src/renderer/src/features/<feature>/; cross-feature imports go through public indexes.

REACT-05.rule: Use the shared UI primitives in src/renderer/src/shared/ and shell/; no raw buttons outside primitive implementations or website templates.

REACT-06.rule: Renderer styles use design tokens: no arbitrary snapped values, raw hex or Tailwind palette colors. The exemption list only shrinks.

REACT-07.rule: React Doctor and React Compiler coverage findings are fixed, not ignored.

TEST-01.rule: Tests live in nearby __tests__/; route-adjacent ones match the router's ignore pattern.

TEST-02.rule: Test behaviour at public seams, mocking only process boundaries; assert outcomes, not mock calls or internals.

TEST-03.rule: Import the subject after vi.mock setup when hoisting could race.

TEST-04.rule: Spawn-heavy tests are integration tests; big module graphs load once in beforeAll.

TEST-06.rule: Each test must cover a branch or kill a mutant no other test does.

TOOL-01.rule: Use TypeScript for tooling and config files when practical; no JavaScript config files.

TOOL-02.rule: No TypeScript baseUrl; use explicit paths entries.

TOOL-04.rule: Outside tests, numeric literals are named SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants.

TOOL-06.rule: Use Bun only: bun install, bun run, bunx. No npm, pnpm, yarn or tsx.

TOOL-07.rule: Change generated files only through their generator command.

TOOL-08.rule: Keep functions, files and branching within the limits in oxlint.config.mts.

TOOL-09.rule: A vendored skill is pinned in skills-lock.json; record each edit with its reason through scripts/skills-lock.ts.

TOOL-10.rule: Promise, `this`, stringify, spread and throw bugs fail lint.

TOOL-11.rule: One spelling for type definitions, array types, optional chains and multi-line bodies.

TOOL-12.rule: Components follow the React Compiler rules.

TOOL-13.rule: Adopted lint rules apply to every file; no per-file rule exemptions.

TOOL-14.rule: A rejected lint rule stays off with its reason and counts in .agents/standards.md.

DEP-01.rule: Direct dependencies and catalog entries are exact versions; `workspace:` and `catalog:` references pass.

DEP-02.rule: Add a dependency only with the user's approval.

DEP-03.rule: A pin that is not the latest release, or has a reason, has a DEPENDENCIES.md row.

DEP-04.rule: A release-age exception names one exact name@version with its reason.

GIT-01.rule: Commits use Conventional Commits: feat, fix, docs, test, chore, refactor, perf, ci, build or revert.

GIT-02.rule: Never skip or disable git hooks, and never force push without the maintainer's approval.

GIT-03.rule: Commit, push, reset, clean, checkout, restore or delete branches only with the maintainer's approval for that action; never overwrite work you did not create.

GATE-01.rule: Fix end-of-turn gate findings before you stop.

GATE-02.rule: Fallow dead-code and duplication findings in changed files are fixed; a false positive gets a commented config entry.

GATE-03.rule: Broken Window: add no warning, suppression, skipped check or skipped test; fix the cause, or change shared config once, with its reason.

GATE-05.rule: Never raise a budget, cap or coverage threshold, or grow an only-shrinks list.

GATE-04.rule: System Resistance: when a tool or type fights a change, fix the design instead of routing around it; a workaround needs a demonstrably wrong tool, reported upstream.

DOC-01.rule: Changing a watched file updates its doc.

DOC-02.rule: User docs in website/src/content/docs follow the write-docs skill and the guide, reference and overview split.

DOC-03.rule: Significant technical findings go in the matching .agents/memory/<topic>.md, within its token cap.

DOC-05.rule: ADR numbers are unique and contiguous, and each ADR is listed in the docs/architecture.md index.
